note: USGS stream gauges on the main rivers into Long Island Sound, west to east. Drainage areas are the gauged area, in square miles. The Naugatuck joins the Housatonic below the Stevenson gauge, so the two add without double counting. On Long Island most fresh water reaches the Sound as groundwater, which stream gauges do not measure.

gauges.name: Bronx River at the New York Botanical Garden
gauges.mouth: the East River at Clason Point, at the Sound's western end
gauges.outlet_note: Set by hand: NHDPlus routes the East River on through New York Harbor, so tracing downstream from the gauge would end below the Hudson.

gauges.name: Nissequogue River near Smithtown
gauges.status_note: USGS has published no flow for this gauge since 4 October 2022, ending a record that began in 1943; the page keeps the record it holds and checks the gauge every hour.

gauges.name: Naugatuck River at Beacon Falls
gauges.mouth: Stratford and Milford, by way of the Housatonic at Derby

gauges.name: Connecticut River at Thompsonville
gauges.status_note: The lowest gauge on the Connecticut with a tide-free flow record; it measures about 86% of the watershed above the mouth (9,660 of about 11,260 square miles). Below Hartford USGS publishes only tidal flow, which reverses with the tide. Values are provisional until USGS approves them.

gauges.mouth: New London, by way of the Thames at Norwich
